summary: Dedicated capacity throughput collapse caused by intermittent GPU slot blocking from background checkpoint writer
description:
Issue summary: Customer Dialogix Health reported a sustained p99/p50 throughput collapse (approx 60% drop) in their Dedicated pool starting 2026-03-13 16:10 UTC. Impact: multiple user-facing endpoints degraded; customer saw increased latency and throttled requests with rising queue lengths.

Environment: Dedicated pool 'dlg-west-2-dedicated' (prod-us-west-2), mixed small-stream and batch routes pinned to gpt-j-6b; autoscaler configured with min=4 max=16 and scale-down cooldown 300s.

Observed behavior: Intermittent GPU slot blocking observed where certain GPU slots remain occupied for long durations (~90-300s) by a node-local process labelled 'checkpoint-writer' causing batching starvation and autoscaler to interpret demand drop and start scale-downs. After scale-down, remaining capacity saturated and p99 latencies spike.

Expected behavior: Background maintenance jobs should be constrained to non-serving slots or throttled such that serving requests maintain expected batching and throughput. Autoscaler should not aggressively scale-down while many slots are soft-blocked.

Customer-visible symptoms: Increased queued request depth, streaming disconnects on long-context streams, sudden 429s as connector enqueued requests hit reservation limits.

Temporary mitigation applied: Isolated node(s) by cordoning the problematic agent, killed the checkpoint-writer process on two nodes, and increased autoscaler cooldown to 900s for the customer's pool to prevent cascading scale-downs while investigation continues.

Follow-up required: Root-cause analysis of why checkpoint writer ran on serving node (recent rollout of node-agent v1.7.3?), autoscaler logic to detect long-running non-serving processes and treat as 'softly-unavailable' rather than indicating lower demand, and customer guidance to run maintenance windows.
steps_to_reproduce: Use a dedicated pool with mixed short-stream and occasional long-batched requests pinned to same GPU type
Deploy node-agent v1.7.3 which contains a background checkpointing task scheduled at random jitter intervals
Generate steady small-stream traffic (50-100 RPS) plus occasional long inference jobs that trigger KV checkpointing
Observe slot occupancy via /internal/slots API and metrics - some slots show >90s continuous occupancy by 'checkpoint-writer' processes
Watch autoscaler behavior - after short drop in observed request completions, autoscaler issues scale-down and capacity removal, causing saturated remaining GPUs and throughput collapse

investigation_notes: Checked /internal/slots; 4 slots showed >120s continuous occupancy with process name 'checkpoint-writer' and CPU usage ~5-10% (I/O bound).

KV-cache metrics stable - this appears unrelated to KV eviction. Memory and GPU utilization on blocked nodes were low, but slot marked unavailable for scheduling due to process holding GPU context lock.
Autoscaler uses completed_requests_per_sec to infer demand; long-running blocking processes reduce observed completions and trigger scale-down prematurely.
Recent node-agent release v1.7.3 introduced a non-nominative maintenance task to flush model checkpoints to NFS with jitter; the task does not check node label or whether slot is serving traffic.
Correlated timeline with customer report and rollout: node-agent v1.7.3 rolled to us-west-2 fleet 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC via canary; rollout completed 2026-03-12 07:40 UTC.
resolution:
Workaround/Short-term: Cordoned affected nodes and killed checkpoint-writer processes; increased autoscaler cooldown to avoid cascading scale-down during transient slot blocking; added temporary runtime label 'maintenance-safe' and patched node-agent to skip checkpoint job on labeled nodes.

Planned long-term actions: Revert the node-agent change that runs maintenance on serving slots (PR revert merged), add a pre-check in node-agent to detect active GPU contexts and avoid taking slots, and improve autoscaler heuristics to detect long-running slot locks and treat them as 'soft-unavailable' so scale-down is suppressed. Add a health-check metric 'slot_block_time' to surface to Console dashboards and create an alert when average slot_block_time > 30s.

Customer follow-up: Dialogix Health to be notified when revert rollout and autoscaler heuristic changes are deployed. Recommend customer schedule any heavy checkpointing or training-related workflows into a maintenance window if they use colocated workloads.
